input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The missing or invalid CA bundle path check in cert_verify emits warnings.warn instead of raising OSError, so the failure no longer stops the request.
- failure path: A user passes verify="/etc/ssl/missing.pem" (or certifi returns an empty path); only a warning is emitted and execution continues to configure the connection with a nonexistent bundle, producing a later, misleading SSL or TypeError at connect time instead of the clear OSError.

Reviewer finding
- description: A missing CA bundle now emits a warning instead of raising OSError, allowing certificate configuration to continue with an invalid path.
- rationale: When an HTTPS request specifies verify='/nonexistent/ca.pem', the existence check reaches this branch. Replacing raise OSError with warnings.warn removes the fail-fast behavior: certificate configuration returns normally and the request proceeds, typically failing later with SSLError instead of the expected OSError. This changes error handling independently of removing the extraction call.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism: cert_verify's missing CA bundle check now calls warnings.warn instead of raising OSError. Execution then continues with the invalid path and fails later with an SSLError. This is exactly the labeled defect.
